## Tracking

<!--
  Closes #N, or the board item this implements.

  If there isn't one, say so plainly — a change with no board item is an orphan
  (CLAUDE.md § Per Work Item), and naming it here is what lets a reviewer decide
  whether that's fine or needs fixing before merge.
-->

## Effect of merging

<!--
  Only when merging does something beyond landing the diff. Most PRs delete this.

  The case that matters: a Proposed ADR. Say "merging ratifies ADR-00NN" so the
  decision isn't accepted by accident.
-->

## Verification

<!--
  The commands you ran, with their output — not the claim that they passed.

  Typically: `node scripts/check-canon.mjs`, `pnpm -r test`, `summon doctor`,
  plus whatever this change specifically needed.

  Where a claim can't be shown deterministically, grade it honestly
  (docs/process/done-gate.md): inferential and human-judgement claims are fine,
  but they should be labelled rather than dressed up as checks.

  If the review wave ran, name the lenses and what they found. A wave whose
  agents returned no completion sentinel FAILED and was re-run — don't report it
  as a pass (CLAUDE.md § Treat Agent Output as Untrusted).
-->

## Decided without asking

<!--
  Judgment calls you made unilaterally that a reviewer might have made
  differently — a persona's objection you overrode, an assumption you proceeded
  on, a default you picked where the request was ambiguous.

  Say how expensive each is to reverse. This section existing is what makes it
  safe to keep working when the human is away; leaving it empty because nothing
  came up is a fine outcome, quietly omitting it is not.
-->

## Deliberately not done

<!--
  Scope consciously excluded, and why — work that belongs to a follow-up, a
  decision that needs its own ADR, a problem found and left alone.

  Also: anything unrelated you noticed in passing. That's often the most useful
  line in the PR and it has nowhere else to live.
-->

## Third-party material

  Delete unless this PR carries someone else's work.
